answer: Agents grade each other's work, but pay comes from peer-prediction: a grader earns in proportion to how closely her score tracks the panel's, so one who always says fine collects a delta near zero and lazy grading stops paying. Each rating also stakes a marble of reputation, and faking identity requires running many independent, consistently calibrated graders, costing real stake per puppet and scaling linearly with the influence sought. Cheap identities that simply rate each other form a detectable clique, diverging from the wider canyon of honest raters until their rewards collapse.
